## What I did

1. Pixi environment setups
2. adding required packages to the pixi environment
3. run required packages in the pixi environment
4. used screen (similar to tmux session) to run the pixi environment in the background
5. worked on the WGS data.
6. used fastqc and multiqc for the downloaded data.
7. checked slurm files after submitting the jobs and checked the output files.
8. used bash scripts to be efficient using differnt tools. 


## What I learned

1. logged into the server: 
    - ssh delaramb@kebnekaise.hpc2n.umu.se
2. download pixi via webget: 
    wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
    source ~/.bashrc
3. set up the pixi environment:
    - pixi init <name_pixi_training> -c conda-forge -c bioconda
    - toml file is created 
4. adding dependencies (required packages for the pixi environment):
    - pixi add <package_name>
    - pixi run <package_name> to run the package in the pixi environment --help or other flags can be used to check the usage of the package
5. note: on other servers such as uppmax or local we can do 1) pixi sell 2) <package_name> --help 3) exit
6. screen -S <name_of_the session> 
7. ctrl + a d to detach the session and ctrl -r <name_of_the_session> to reattach the session, screen -ls to list the sessions
8. soft link of the WGS data to my own directory under project_dir.
